chapter: Boston, Buffalo and finding a style
title: Peanuts Holland's trumpet idols and the band's keys and members
summary: Holland admired Armstrong, Rex Stewart, Cootie Williams and Hot Lips Page; Stewart still played by ear in three keys and recalls only altoist Don Stovall.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Okay, all right. Now, in that band were they playing, Peanuts Holland, who did he like? Who were his idols that he taught you about, the guys that really liked he -- what did he play, by the way?
He played trumpet.
He was a trumpeter.
He was quite a trumpeter, yes.
Who did he like? Did he like Louis Armstrong or --
Oh, yes, Louis and quite a few of the trumpet players coming up at that time.
Like Rex Stewart.
Rex, right.
Cootie Williams?
Cootie.
Walter Page?
Walter Page?
I mean Hot Lips Page.
Hot Lips, oh, yes, Hot Lips.
Right, Hot Lips Page, yeah.
Well, it's real surprising. There were quite a few trumpeters that came around during those years.
Were you -- were the things that you had to play in the band, did they have written charts for you or did you -- were you still playing by ear?
Still playing by ear, yes.
Were they, was this band too only playing like for two or three keys like C and B flat and F?
That's right.
They were basically in those three keys?
Basically, yes.
Okay. Now, were there any people in that band who later became well known players, in this Peanuts Holland band?
Not that I -- I don't quite remember. I know Peanuts, that years later he played with Count Basie and what have you. But as far as the other members, the saxophone
x no. Charlie Barnet, Don Redman. Cob Collogay's small band

player, alto sax, his name was Don Stovall, and, of course, as the years went on by, you lose track of these fellows. But Peanuts, he was quite a trumpeter, and you heard more about him as the years went by. And I hadn't even left the band to venture further, further near home, that is.
